AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we cover a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. To keep off rain and sun
   B. To hide it from animals only
   C. To make it heavier
   D. To stop it from rotting

2. Who should make holes in bottle caps and pipes with a nail? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher or an adult
   B. A small child alone
   C. Anyone with wet hands
   D. Nobody

3. What is the best time of day to water crops? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. Noon
   C. Early morning or late afternoon
   D. Midnight only

4. Which of these is a way of collecting water for the garden? (1 mark)
   A. Collecting rainwater from a roof
   B. Cutting down trees
   C. Digging up rivers
   D. Burning the roof

5. Why is the water container placed on a stand? (1 mark)
   A. So water flows down through the pipe
   B. To keep it out of the sun forever
   C. To hide it from birds
   D. So it looks tall

6. Why should the holes in a drip pipe be tiny? (1 mark)
   A. So water drips slowly
   B. So water pours out fast
   C. So the water is warm
   D. So the pipe becomes lighter

7. Which fuel comes in a metal cylinder? (1 mark)
   A. Gas
   B. Dung cakes
   C. Firewood
   D. Charcoal

8. What is a drill in sowing? (1 mark)
   A. A type of seed
   B. A power tool
   C. A weed
   D. A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown

9. Which tool is used to make the soil fine and level? (1 mark)
   A. Hammer
   B. Panga
   C. Spade only for cutting trees
   D. Rake

10. Why are carrots not transplanted? (1 mark)
   A. They have no roots
   B. Moving damages the root and makes it crooked
   C. They grow in water
   D. They are too large

11. Which is a woody tree fruit in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Tree tomato
   B. Raspberry
   C. Grapes
   D. Kiwi

12. What is a tree tomato? (1 mark)
   A. A climbing vine
   B. A cereal
   C. A vegetable that grows underground
   D. A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands

13. Why should the soil be firmed around a newly planted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To make the plant fall
   C. To remove air spaces and hold the roots
   D. To dry the roots

14. What is pruning? (1 mark)
   A. Watering the plant
   B. Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches
   C. Harvesting fruit
   D. Planting a seed

15. Which product comes from a hen? (1 mark)
   A. Wool
   B. Leather
   C. Eggs
   D. Honey

16. Which group does githeri belong to mainly? (1 mark)
   A. Only protective
   B. Drinks
   C. Energy and body-building
   D. Only water

17. What is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. A meal with foods from all the main groups in the right amounts
   B. A very large meal
   C. A meal with only one kind of food
   D. A meal of only sweets

18. Which of these meals is balanced? (1 mark)
   A. Chips only
   B. Tea and bread only
   C. Soda and sweets
   D. Ugali, beans and sukuma wiki

19. Why is a food journal kept for a week? (1 mark)
   A. To find cheap shops
   B. To check whether meals are balanced
   C. To improve handwriting only
   D. To count the number of plates

20. Which meal is missing body-building foods? (1 mark)
   A. Rice, beans and cabbage
   B. Ugali and sukuma wiki only
   C. Chapati, egg and tomato
   D. Ugali, fish and spinach

21. Why should the frying pan be heated before adding food? (1 mark)
   A. So that food browns and does not soak up oil
   B. To melt it
   C. To burn it
   D. To break it

22. What should you do before you start cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Play with the fire
   B. Eat first
   C. Wash your hands
   D. Take off your shoes

23. How often should you brush your teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Once a year
   B. Once a month
   C. Twice a day
   D. Never

24. Why is a tippy tap useful? (1 mark)
   A. It makes soap
   B. It cleans clothes
   C. It needs electricity
   D. It works without a water tap and saves water

25. In which direction do you sweep a room? (1 mark)
   A. Only along the walls
   B. Only the middle
   C. Randomly
   D. From the corners towards the middle or door

26. What is personal protective equipment? (1 mark)
   A. Tools for digging
   B. Soap for cleaning
   C. Food for health
   D. Clothing and gear worn to protect the body

27. Why stuff canvas shoes with paper after washing? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them dirty
   B. It makes them heavier
   C. It makes them wet
   D. It keeps their shape and soaks up moisture

28. Where should canvas shoes be dried? (1 mark)
   A. Under wet clothes
   B. In a sealed box
   C. In a fire
   D. In an airy, shady place

29. What should you do with laces when cleaning canvas shoes? (1 mark)
   A. Cut them
   B. Leave them dirty
   C. Remove and wash them separately
   D. Burn them

30. What is a tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. A temporary stitch that holds cloth in place
   B. A type of cloth
   C. A permanent decorative stitch
   D. A cutting tool

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how to plant a fruit seedling. (4 marks)

32. Explain three safety rules when cleaning. (3 marks)

33. Describe the first aid for a small burn. (3 marks)

34. Describe how to care for a seedbed after sowing. (4 marks)

35. What should you do after cooking to keep the kitchen safe and clean? (2 marks)

36. Why do we need protective foods? (2 marks)

37. Name the three main food groups and one example of each. (3 marks)

38. What is meant by coexisting with wild animals? (2 marks)

39. Write the steps for preparing a meal using both boiling and shallow frying. Include hygiene and safety. (5 marks)

40. Plan a group project of making a scarecrow shirt using tacking. Give materials, steps, safety and how the group shares work. (5 marks)

41. Describe how to make a tippy tap. (4 marks)

42. Explain three mistakes to avoid when tacking. (3 marks)

43. Why is poison or a trap not a good way of dealing with wild animals? (4 marks)

44. Explain what drip irrigation is. (2 marks)

45. Describe how to mop a floor. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — To keep off rain and sun
   A cover protects the heap from too much rain and drying sun.

2. A — A teacher or an adult
   Nails and awls are sharp and can cause injuries.

3. C — Early morning or late afternoon
   The sun is less hot, so less water evaporates.

4. A — Collecting rainwater from a roof
   Rainwater tanks store water for dry days.

5. A — So water flows down through the pipe
   A raised container gives water the push to flow down.

6. A — So water drips slowly
   Small holes give slow drips that soak into the soil.

7. A — Gas
   LPG gas is stored under pressure in a cylinder.

8. D — A shallow line in the soil where seeds are sown
   A drill is a shallow furrow made with a stick.

9. D — Rake
   A rake breaks lumps and levels the bed.

10. B — Moving damages the root and makes it crooked
   The carrot root is the food, so it must grow straight.

11. A — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato and guava are woody.

12. D — A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   Tree tomato is a woody tree fruit.

13. C — To remove air spaces and hold the roots
   Air pockets dry out roots.

14. B — Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches
   Pruning helps light and air reach the plant.

15. C — Eggs
   Hens lay eggs.

16. C — Energy and body-building
   Maize gives energy, beans give protein.

17. A — A meal with foods from all the main groups in the right amounts
   A balanced meal includes energy, body-building and protective foods.

18. D — Ugali, beans and sukuma wiki
   It includes all three groups.

19. B — To check whether meals are balanced
   A journal shows patterns in eating.

20. B — Ugali and sukuma wiki only
   Ugali and kale give energy and vitamins but no protein food.

21. A — So that food browns and does not soak up oil
   Food placed in cold oil soaks up oil.

22. C — Wash your hands
   Clean hands prevent germs.

23. C — Twice a day
   Morning and before bed.

24. D — It works without a water tap and saves water
   It can be made from a jerrican.

25. D — From the corners towards the middle or door
   This gathers dirt in one place.

26. D — Clothing and gear worn to protect the body
   PPE protects us from harm.

27. D — It keeps their shape and soaks up moisture
   Paper absorbs water.

28. D — In an airy, shady place
   Gentle drying protects the shoes.

29. C — Remove and wash them separately
   Laces need to be washed too.

30. A — A temporary stitch that holds cloth in place
   Tacking is removed later.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water the seedling; remove the bag carefully; place at the same depth in the hole; fill with soil and firm; water and mulch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four correct steps.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not mix chemicals; keep chemicals from children; wear gloves for dirty work; do not leave floors wet (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the burn under cool running clean water for at least ten minutes, cover it loosely with a clean cloth and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water gently and regularly, remove weeds, thin the seedlings, and protect the bed from animals and birds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put out the fire or switch off the gas, wash and store utensils and wipe the working area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fire or gas, 1 mark for cleaning.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins and minerals that fight sickness and keep the body healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fight sickness, 1 mark for vitamins or minerals.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy-giving: ugali; body-building: beans; protective: sukuma wiki (or other correct examples).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with example.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: Living together peacefully so that both farmers and animals are safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for living together, 1 mark for both safe.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands; wash food; boil potatoes until soft; shallow fry an egg or fish; serve with vegetables; safety: adult present, handles inward, dry cloth, water away from hot oil; clean up after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for hygiene, 1 for boiling, 1 for frying, 1 for safety, 1 for serving and cleaning.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: old cloth, needles, thread, scissors, chalk, ruler. Steps: measure and cut two pieces; pin; tack along sides; leave openings; sew firmly; stuff. Safety: count needles. Group: share tools, assign jobs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark materials, 2 marks steps, 1 mark safety, 1 mark teamwork.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Take a clean jerrican; make a small hole near the cap; hang it; tie a string from the cap to a foot lever; place a basin below and hang soap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Uneven stitches, pulling the thread too tight, using thread the same colour as the cloth, making a hard knot at the end (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mistake.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: It can kill other animals, pets and people, it hurts animals, and it harms nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason, up to 4.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is watering plants slowly, drop by drop, next to their roots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for slowly or drop by drop, 1 mark for near the roots.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sweep first; fill a bucket with clean soapy water; squeeze the mop; start from the far corner and mop backwards to the door; rinse the mop; leave the floor to dry with a warning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.
